nonclaims: No time-dependent entropy or pointwise PDE claim.
No arbitrary supplied operator or measure identification.
objects_and_scopes: For every n,N in Nat: E is real Euclidean space of dimension n+1, S its unit sphere, and M=Fin N -> S with induced stereographic/product smooth structures. No positivity restriction on n or N.

tau is the polar sphere measure derived from Euclidean volume; sigma=(tau univ)^(-1) times tau, in ENNReal measure scaling; mu is its finite product. Strictly positive finite tau mass and probability are derived, not assumptions.
Radial extension normalizes nonzero vectors and is zero at the origin. Every operator is evaluated at a unit point; regularity at the artificial origin is neither assumed nor used.

The gradient is the tangent orthogonal projection of the actual Euclidean gradient of that extension; divergence is the actual coordinate trace. Product operators use coordinate replacement and an unaveraged finite sum.

The main inputs are arbitrary real C1 f and ambient-valued C1 components V_i on the full product, with pointwise tangency at every x,i. The weighted inputs are arbitrary real C1 f,rho and C2 g; rho need not be nonnegative or normalized.

Conclusions are three real-integrability assertions, zero total divergence integral, and the signed integration-by-parts identity. The specialization uses the literal field rho times grad_i g. These are static finite real integrals, not time-a.e. identities.

proof_nodes.claim: Derive canonical radial C1/C2 regularity on the product of punctured ambient spaces from intrinsic charts; extension agreement and tangent differentiation hold on the sphere.
Radial derivative in the radius direction vanishes; the Riesz representative pairs with tangent velocities as the intrinsic differential, and the ambient trace reduces to the induced tangent trace.

Construct an annular compactly supported ambient C1 field. Ambient zero-divergence plus polar integration yields a nonzero scalar radial factor times the sphere divergence integral; tangency cancels the cutoff derivative and the scalar factor is cancelled.
Actual derivative product rule and tangency identify div(fV)=<grad f,V>+f div V. Compactness supplies finite integrability and T3 yields single-sphere IBP.
Normalize explicit sphere mass; derive continuity/integrability of coordinate sections on the compact product; finite-product Fubini and finite sums yield the main theorem including N=0.
Full parameter-dependent derivative calculus gives C1 coordinate gradients from C2 g; projection yields tangency. Multiply by C1 rho and substitute in T5, with scalar-inner-product algebra.

required_bridges_to_check_in_implementat: Intrinsic-to-radial regularity must be proved, including coordinate parameters; a supplied ambient extension premise does not discharge this contract.
The radial cutoff scalar must actually be positive/nonzero; no informal cancellation of a zero or infinite real factor.
Finite integrability must precede use of integral sums/Fubini; totalized Lean integrals cannot substitute for these conclusions.
Intrinsic gradient pairing and tangent trace identification must be actual derived formulas, not comments or names.
Zero sphere dimension and empty product must follow the stated formulas; no hidden n>0/N>0 or subtraction truncation.
